e-491.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
e-491.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv' \, \textrm{d}x= uv - \int vu' \, \textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle  \int xe^{7x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle  \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{7x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}-\int \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}\int {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}(\frac{{e}^{7x}}{7})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{49}{e}^{7x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-492.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
e-492.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv'\,\textrm{d}x= uv- \int vu'\,\textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle \int x \cos{2x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\int \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-6209.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
e-6209.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-\int (-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+{\frac{1}{5}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\frac{1}{5}\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)]+[\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =[-\frac{\pi }{25}\cdot (-1)+0]+[0-0] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate the integral ∫(x−2)ex+3dx.

a
(x3−6)ex+3+C
b
(xln⁡3+3)ex+3+C
c
(x−3)ex+3+C
d
(x2−3)ex+3+C
e
(2x−1)ex+3+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x-2 and dv=e^{x+3} dx gives (x-2)e^{x+3}-e^{x+3}+C=(x-3)e^{x+3}+C. Differentiating yields (x-2)e^{x+3}, confirming option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x-2){e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x-2\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{x+3}\, & ⟹\,v={e}^{x+3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x-2)\cdot {e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x & =(x-2)\cdot {e}^{x+3}-\int {e}^{x+3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x-2){e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x & =(x-2){e}^{x+3}-\int {e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x-2){e}^{x+3}-{e}^{x+3}+C \\  & =(x-3){e}^{x+3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate the integral ∫(x−2)ex+3dx.

a
(x3−6)ex+3+C
b
(xln⁡3+3)ex+3+C
c
(x−3)ex+3+C
d
(x2−3)ex+3+C
e
(2x−1)ex+3+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(x−2)ex+3dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x−2⟹u′=1v′=ex+3⟹v=ex+3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(x−2)⋅ex+3dx=(x−2)⋅ex+3−∫ex+3⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(x−2)ex+3dx=(x−2)ex+3−∫ex+3dx=(x−2)ex+3−ex+3+C=(x−3)ex+3+C

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms integration by parts gives (x-2)e^{x+3}-e^{x+3}+C=(x-3)e^{x+3}+C, matching option c. Its derivative is (x-2)e^{x+3}.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x-2){e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x-2\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{x+3}\, & ⟹\,v={e}^{x+3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x-2)\cdot {e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x & =(x-2)\cdot {e}^{x+3}-\int {e}^{x+3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x-2){e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x & =(x-2){e}^{x+3}-\int {e}^{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x-2){e}^{x+3}-{e}^{x+3}+C \\  & =(x-3){e}^{x+3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=6x and dv=e^{4x} dx gives (3x/2)e^{4x}-(3/2)∫e^{4x} dx=(3x/2)e^{4x}-(3/8)e^{4x}+C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{4x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}-\int \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{4x}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{4x}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

∫6xe4xdx=

a
3xe4x2−3e4x8+C
b
e4x3+e4x9+C
c
xe4x2−3e4x8+C
d
xe4x3+xe4x9+C
e
3xe4x2−3e4x9+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫6xe4xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=6x⟹u′=6v′=e4x⟹v=14e4x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫6x⋅e4xdx=6x⋅14e4x−∫14e4x⋅6dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫6xe4xdx=32xe4x−32∫e4xdx=3xe4x2−3e4x8+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{4x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}-\int \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{4x}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{4x}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫(3x−4)e−3xdx.

a
(2−x)e−3x3+C
b
(2x−1)e−3x3+C
c
(2−3x)e−3x+C
d
(2x−1)e−3x+C
e
(1−x)e−3x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=3x-4 and v=-e^{-3x}/3 gives -(3x-4)e^{-3x}/3-e^{-3x}/3+C=(1-x)e^{-3x}+C. Differentiating gives (3x-4)e^{-3x}, confirming option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x-4\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x-4)\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x-4)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}+\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =-\frac{(3x-3){e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =(1-x){e}^{-3x}+C\end{aligned}

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫(3x−4)e−3xdx.

a
(2−x)e−3x3+C
b
(2x−1)e−3x3+C
c
(2−3x)e−3x+C
d
(2x−1)e−3x+C
e
(1−x)e−3x+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(3x−4)e−3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x−4⟹u′=3v′=e−3x⟹v=−e−3x3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(3x−4)⋅e−3xdx=(3x−4)⋅(−e−3x3)−∫(−e−3x3)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(3x−4)e−3xdx=−(3x−4)e−3x3+∫e−3xdx=−(3x−4)e−3x3−e−3x3+C=−(3x−3)e−3x3+C=(1−x)e−3x+C

verification.explanation: The revealed solution gives -(3x-4)e^{-3x}/3-e^{-3x}/3+C=(1-x)e^{-3x}+C. Its derivative is [-1-3(1-x)]e^{-3x}=(3x-4)e^{-3x}, confirming option e.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x-4\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x-4)\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x-4)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}+\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =-\frac{(3x-3){e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =(1-x){e}^{-3x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate ∫(3x+5)e−5xdx.

a
−3xe−5x25−3e−5x25+C
b
(3x+5)e−5x5+3xe−5x25+C
c
(3x+5)e−5x25−e−5x5+C
d
−(3x+5)e5x5+3xe5x25+C
e
−(3x+5)e−5x5−3e−5x25+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=3x+5 and v=-e^{-5x}/5 gives -(3x+5)e^{-5x}/5+(3/5)∫e^{-5x} dx=-(3x+5)e^{-5x}/5-3e^{-5x}/25+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+5\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-5x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x+5)\cdot {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x+5)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}+\frac{3}{5}\int {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}-\frac{3{e}^{-5x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate ∫(3x+5)e−5xdx.

a
−3xe−5x25−3e−5x25+C
b
(3x+5)e−5x5+3xe−5x25+C
c
(3x+5)e−5x25−e−5x5+C
d
−(3x+5)e5x5+3xe5x25+C
e
−(3x+5)e−5x5−3e−5x25+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(3x+5)e−5xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x+5⟹u′=3v′=e−5x⟹v=−e−5x5.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(3x+5)⋅e−5xdx=(3x+5)⋅(−e−5x5)−∫(−e−5x5)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(3x+5)e−5xdx=−(3x+5)e−5x5+35∫e−5xdx=−(3x+5)e−5x5−3e−5x25+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+5\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-5x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x+5)\cdot {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x+5)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}+\frac{3}{5}\int {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}-\frac{3{e}^{-5x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

a

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=4x and v=e^{8x}/8 gives xe^{8x}/2-(1/2)∫e^{8x} dx=xe^{8x}/2-e^{8x}/16+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 4x{e}^{8x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{8x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}-\int \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x{e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x{e}^{8x}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{8x}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{8x}}{16}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

∫4xe8xdx=

a
 xe8x8−e8x16+C
b
 xe8x2−e8x4+C
c
 3xe8x8+e8x12+C
d
 xe8x2−e8x16+C
e
xe8x4+5e8x16+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫4xe8xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=4x⟹u′=4v′=e8x⟹v=18e8x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫4x⋅e8xdx=4x⋅18e8x−∫18e8x⋅4dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫4xe8xdx=12xe8x−12∫e8xdx=xe8x2−e8x16+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 4x{e}^{8x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{8x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}-\int \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x{e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x{e}^{8x}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{8x}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{8x}}{16}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x+4 and v=-cos(2x)/2 gives -(x+4)cos(2x)/2+(1/2)∫cos(2x) dx=-(x+4)cos(2x)/2+sin(2x)/4+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x+4\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x+4)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =(x+4)\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x & =-\frac{(x+4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(x+4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(x+4)sin⁡(2x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x+4⟹u′=1v′=sin⁡(2x)⟹v=−cos⁡(2x)2.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(x+4)⋅sin⁡(2x)dx=(x+4)⋅(−cos⁡(2x)2)−∫(−cos⁡(2x)2)⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(x+4)sin⁡(2x)dx=−(x+4)cos⁡(2x)2+12∫cos⁡(2x)dx=−(x+4)cos⁡(2x)2+sin⁡(2x)4+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x+4\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x+4)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =(x+4)\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x & =-\frac{(x+4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(x+4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Calculate ∫5xsin⁡(x)dx.

a
5xcos⁡x−xsin⁡x+C
b
−xcos⁡x−cos⁡5x+C
c
cos⁡5x+xsin⁡5x+C
d
−5xsin⁡x+cos⁡x+C
e
−5xcos⁡x+5sin⁡x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=5x and v=-cos(x) gives -5x cos(x)+5∫cos(x) dx=-5x cos(x)+5sin(x)+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 5\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

a
5xcos⁡x−xsin⁡x+C
b
−xcos⁡x−cos⁡5x+C
c
cos⁡5x+xsin⁡5x+C
d
−5xsin⁡x+cos⁡x+C
e
−5xcos⁡x+5sin⁡x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫5xsin⁡(x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=5x⟹u′=5v′=sin⁡(x)⟹v=−cos⁡(x).

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫5x⋅sin⁡(x)dx=5x⋅(−cos⁡(x))−∫(−cos⁡(x))⋅5dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫5xsin⁡(x)dx=−5xcos⁡(x)+5∫cos⁡(x)dx=−5xcos⁡(x)+5sin⁡(x)+C

content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 5\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (6x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x+1\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (6x+1)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =(6x+1)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (6x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =(6x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(6x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

b

c

e
 sin⁡(x)+cos⁡(x)+C

EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(6x+1)cos⁡(x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=6x+1⟹u′=6v′=cos⁡(x)⟹v=sin⁡(x).

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(6x+1)⋅cos⁡(x)dx=(6x+1)⋅sin⁡(x)−∫sin⁡(x)⋅6dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows

∫(6x+1)cos⁡(x)dx=(6x+1)sin⁡(x)−6∫sin⁡(x)dx=(6x+1)sin⁡(x)+6cos⁡(x)+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (6x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x+1\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (6x+1)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =(6x+1)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (6x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =(6x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(6x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Calculate ∫2xcos⁡4xdx.

a
 −sin⁡4x8+xcos⁡4x2+C
b
 −sin⁡4x4+xcos⁡4x6+C
c
 3xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x4+C
d
 xsin⁡4x4−cos⁡4x2+C
e
 xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x8+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=2x and v=sin(4x)/4 gives x sin(4x)/2-(1/2)∫sin(4x) dx=x sin(4x)/2+cos(4x)/8+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\int \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Calculate ∫2xcos⁡4xdx.

a
 −sin⁡4x8+xcos⁡4x2+C
b
 −sin⁡4x4+xcos⁡4x6+C
c
 3xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x4+C
d
 xsin⁡4x4−cos⁡4x2+C
e
 xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x8+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫2xcos⁡4xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=2x⟹u′=2v′=cos⁡4x⟹v=14sin⁡4x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫2xcos⁡4xdx=2x⋅14sin⁡4x−∫14sin⁡4x⋅2dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫2xcos⁡4xdx=12xsin⁡4x−12∫sin⁡4xdx=12xsin⁡4x−12(−14cos⁡4x)+C=12xsin⁡4x+18cos⁡4x+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\int \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x))-\int (-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)}{4}+\frac{1}{4}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & ={-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)}{4}|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)}{4}|}_{0}^{\pi }+{\frac{1}{16}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =[-\frac{\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(4\pi )}{4}+\frac{0\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot 0)}{4}] \\  & +\frac{1}{16}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0)] \\  & =(-\frac{\pi }{4}+0)+\frac{1}{16}(0-0) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
